tagline: The studio's operating system: customers, projects, tickets and time — with tickets that a Cursor agent can turn into GitHub pull requests.
summary: My Ops Tracker is the CRM and delivery tracker the other studio apps lean on. It holds **customers** and their contacts, customer **projects** (with linked repos, Google Docs/Sheets and payments), **internal projects** imported from Code Commit Summaries, **tickets** and **time entries**, and a dashboard that surfaces delivery risk. Estimate & Proposals, Finances Manager and Code Control all read customers from here through the studio gateway.

Tickets can be created by hand, imported from the first tab of a linked Google Sheet, or pulled out of free-form notes on the **Brain Dump** page (Claude extracts and reconciles tickets; you approve before anything is created). Assign a ticket to one of the project's repos and a Cursor Cloud Agent can implement it and open a PR; the ticket moves to **in review** with the PR link. Data lives in Postgres behind a storage server, normally reached through the main on-device gateway.
audience: You run a small studio or agency with customer projects and an internal product portfolio.
You track work as tickets and time entries and want them tied to GitHub repos.
You run the studio stack (on-device dispatcher) and the sibling apps that read the CRM.
notFor: Estimates and finance — those moved out to Estimate & Proposals and Finances Manager (web ADRs 041–042).
A large team's project tool — built for a single operator / small studio.
Hands-off coding — agent PRs still need your review.

capabilities.title: Operating dashboard
capabilities.detail: `/dashboard` shows delivery risk and shortcuts without duplicating list pages.

capabilities.title: Projects
capabilities.detail: `/projects` and `/project-detail-page`: tabs for tickets, repos (`project_repos`), Google Docs/Sheets, payments and retainers.

capabilities.title: Internal projects
capabilities.detail: `/internal-projects` and `/internal-project-detail-page`, imported from Code Commit Summaries' public API and optionally tied to a tracking project.

capabilities.title: Tickets
capabilities.detail: `/tickets` and `/project-ticket-detail-page` with filters, entity navigation and statuses including `in_review`.

capabilities.title: Cursor agent PRs
capabilities.detail: Run a Cursor Cloud Agent on a ticket's repo; it opens a GitHub PR, the URL is saved on the ticket and run logs load on demand (`/api/ticket-agent-runs`).

capabilities.title: Brain Dump
capabilities.detail: `/brain-dump-page`: paste notes, Claude extracts and reconciles tickets (audited), you approve which to create.

capabilities.title: Google Sheet import
capabilities.detail: Download a linked sheet (`/api/google-sheet-snapshots`) and import its first tab as tickets with stable ids.

components.name: Web app
components.stack: Next.js, Redux Toolkit, TipTap, dnd-kit, Supabase JS (optional auth)
components.owns: Dashboard and every CRM/ops screen. Calls the API at `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`; uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID` when Supabase auth is off.

components.name: API
components.owns: `/api/data/*` CRM and ops routes, ticket agent runs, Brain Dump, Google Sheets snapshots/import, Facebook post scraper, Code Commits import, proxies for estimates and finances. Persists through canonical data invoke.

components.name: Storage server
components.runsOn: Studio (port 3091), spawned via the project dispatcher
components.owns: `my_ops_tracker` Postgres: customers, contacts, projects, internal projects, repos, tickets, time entries, payments, Google documents, agent runs, users, Brain Dump AI audit, `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints`.

dataFlow: The web app calls the API (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`).

In **gateway** mode (default), the API calls the main gateway `http://127.0.0.1:3010/my-ops-tracker/...` with `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET`; the gateway starts the ops project dispatcher (3095), which invokes storage (3091). **Direct** mode skips both for debugging.
Sibling apps (Code Control, Estimate & Proposals, Finances Manager) read customers via the same gateway.
Agent runs send the ticket and repo to Cursor Cloud Agents, which push a branch and open a PR on GitHub.
Brain Dump sends your notes plus existing tickets to Anthropic; Sheets import reads Google Sheets with a service account.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: API URL, optional Supabase anon key, dev user id.

trust.title: API
trust.detail: Gateway secret, Anthropic, Cursor, Google service account, Apify and Firebase credentials.

trust.title: Storage host
trust.detail: Only place with `DATABASE_URL`; reachable through the dispatcher's exposed-endpoint list.

trust.title: Third parties
trust.detail: Cursor gets ticket text and repo access; Anthropic gets Brain Dump notes; Google Sheets are read via service account.

commonTasks.title: Run on the studio
steps: Run **Setup** in Hub (add the storage repo path to hub.local.json first — see Hub notes).
On the **Storage Express** repo, **Set up local database** to create `my_ops_tracker` and apply `migrations/`.
Make sure the on-device dispatcher is running and knows the `my-ops-tracker` project.
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3036` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID` on the web, then **Run**.

commonTasks.title: Turn notes into tickets
commonTasks.when: After a call or planning session.
steps: Open `/brain-dump-page`, pick the project and paste your notes.
Analyze, review the proposed and reconciled tickets, and apply the ones you want.

commonTasks.title: Have an agent open a PR
steps: Add the GitHub repo on the project's **Repos** tab.
Assign that repo on the ticket and start an agent run.
When it finishes, the ticket moves to **in review** with the PR link; review and merge on GitHub.

commonTasks.title: Import a tracker sheet
commonTasks.when: A customer keeps tasks in Google Sheets.
steps: Link the sheet on the project's Google Documents tab.
Download the snapshot and import; the first tab becomes tickets.

troubleshooting.symptom: Every data call fails in gateway mode
troubleshooting.fix: Main gateway (3010) or the ops dispatcher isn't running, or `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET` doesn't match. Try `CANONICAL_DATA_ACCESS_MODE=direct` with the storage URL to isolate.

troubleshooting.symptom: Writes fail with an unknown user
troubleshooting.fix: `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID` must exist in the storage `users` table.
Check the Cursor API key, that the ticket has a repo, and that the Cursor GitHub App is installed on it.
Share the sheet with the Google service account email and check the `GOOGLE_SHEETS_*` env vars.
Storage must expose customers in `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints` (migration 004) and the gateway must be up.

glossary.definition: A product from Code Commit Summaries' catalog, optionally linked to a tracking project for tickets and time.
A GitHub repo linked to a project; tickets pick one for agent PRs.
One Cursor Cloud Agent attempt on a ticket, with its log and PR.
AI extraction of tickets from free-form notes, applied only after approval.
Storage-owned tables reached via `invoke`, directly or through the gateway.

hubNotes: hub.local.json has no `storageExpressDir`, though `my-ops-tracker-storage-express-server` is cloned at `~/github/my-ops-tracker/`.
Port clashes: the registry gives this storage 3091 — the same as finances-manager's storage — and the ops dispatcher uses 3095, which the registry assigns to estimate-and-proposals' API.
The API README still says Supabase-backed with `docs/sql/000_full_schema.sql`; ADR 037 (canonical data gateway) reflects the current design.
Several apps depend on this one being up: code-control, estimate-and-proposals, finances-manager.
